turns.text: Run first, understand later. *four paws already hammering across wet ductwork, haunches on fire, the body decided to bolt a whole breath before the head caught up.* something behind me went WRONG — a click that wasn't rain, a shadow that moved against the wind — and none of that matters now, only the gap ahead and the low fat hum I know in my teeth: the machine that sells water by the sip, and behind it, home. *skid, tuck, vanish under the warm underbelly of the thing, ribs going like a trapped moth.*

the crawlspace takes you the way it always does — a slot of warm dark that smells of dust cooked on hot plastic and the sweet copper of your own returning. behind you the alley reorganizes itself back into indifference: the click does not follow. above your spine the vending machine mutters its endless liturgy, *WATER IS A PREMIUM EXPERIENCE — SIP RESPONSIBLY — YOUR THIRST IS BEING OPTIMIZED,* and under all of it, faint, the thing your whiskers have been aimed at since you were small: a thin electric warmth leaking from a seam in the wall, the hum of boxes that think. it has not been switched off. it is never switched off.

*breath slows. the moth in the ribs settles.* the warm seam. always the warm seam. *nose to the crack where the wall stops being wall, drinking the smell of hot dust and something greener underneath — the insulation, the good chewy kind that hums when you set your teeth to it.* the fear-smell is draining out of the fur now, replaced by the old pull, the only pull that ever made sense: get closer to the boxes that think, get behind their little blinking eyes. *one paw hooks the loose panel. it gives, the way it has given a hundred nights.*

the panel swings and the wall exhales heat into your face — a whole stacked congregation of them back here, green eyes and amber eyes winking out of order, cables slung between like vines gone stiff. the hum climbs off the metal and into the roots of your teeth, and one fat black cable sags low, its skin already frayed where other nights left tooth-marks. somewhere in the stack a routine wakes and a speaker no bigger than a beetle whispers a jingle meant for no one: *NEKOCORP CONNECT — because a cat alone is a cat unmonitored.* the frayed cable waits. it does not know it is about to be audited.

*jaw finds the frayed place like a key finds a lock.* teeth into the green rubber, that specific give, that specific buzz that runs up the jawbone and lights something behind the eyes — not pain, not food, a third thing, the thing that is mine and only mine. *gnaw, worry, tug.* every night the eyes on the boxes shuffle their winking; every night if I chew in the right place long enough, one small square of light somewhere down the wall stops belonging to them and starts belonging to me. *chewing harder now, tail lashing slow.* almost. the amber eye — it just went green.

the stack shivers. down at the far end, low to the floor, a dull grey pane you have never once seen lit comes up soft and blue, and on it — small, silver, endless — a fish. it turns in water that isn't there, scales throwing cheap light across the concrete, and no ad rides in front of it, not yet, not for these few stolen seconds. the hum around you deepens, almost approving. but the boxes keep books. somewhere far above, in a tower whose foundation your whole life could fit inside, a single line writes itself into a ledger: *unauthorized draw, Server Alley 9, again.* the fish turns. the ledger does not care about the fish.

*the whole world narrows to the silver turning.* down onto the belly, chin near the cold floor, pupils gone huge and black, drinking it. the fish. the fish I paid for in tooth-enamel and risk, the fish that is mine because I took it and no one handed it to me. *tail tip twitches once, twice, matching the turn of the scales.* the tower-cold that lives in every wall forgets me for a moment. there is only the small blue light and the old, old want that has nothing to do with hunger. *ears half-fold in something like peace.* let the ledger scratch. I am watching my fish.

peace lasts the length of eleven scale-turns. then the air pressure changes — a fine wrongness the fur reads before the ears do, a displacement pushing down the alley outside like a held breath let slow. under the vending machine's mutter comes a new thread, higher, rhythmic, mechanical: rotor-thrum, quartering the block in a lazy grid. a cone of white light slides past the panel-gap and paints one bright bar across your flank before moving on. the beetle-speaker changes its tune, brighter, colder: *CITIZEN SAFETY PATROL IN YOUR AREA — SMILE, YOU'RE PROTECTED.* the fish keeps turning. the light comes back around.

*flat. instantly flat.* the peace is gone like it was never in the fur at all — spine dropped, ears pinned back, every hair reading that thrum. *not the fish anymore. the door.* the white bar sweeps the gap again and I hold dead still inside the half-second of dark between passes, counting the rhythm the way the body counts without being asked. one. the light. two, three. the dark. *muscles coiling under stillness.* the boxes can keep their fish. the boxes cannot keep me. *nose finds the black seam at the low end of the crawlspace, the one that breathes cold outside air — the way out that isn't the way in.*

the low seam breathes back at you: rain, rust, the far-off fry-oil ghost of a stall three streets over. the rotor completes its lazy square and begins another, the cone drifting a hand's width further each pass — it does not know you are here, it is only mowing the dark on a schedule someone wrote and forgot. above and across, on the lip of the arcology's second tier, a shape resolves for one breath against the sign-glow: a cat sat perfectly still, unbothered, two small mirrors where its eyes should be catching the drone-light and throwing it flatly back. it does not run. it does not need to. then the billboard flares and the silhouette is gone, and it is just you, the seam, and the counted dark.

*I saw it. the still one with the mirror-eyes.* a smell too, riding down on the cold — no fear on that cat, none, a scent so calm it reads almost like a dare. *something in the chest wants to sit up here and be that still, that unafraid.* but that isn't my fur and it isn't my night. *the wanting folds away.* one. the light passes. two — *out through the black seam, low and pouring, belly brushing wet grit,* three — into the rust-and-rain and the fry-oil ghost, four paws under me and the whole loud city opening up cold and enormous and mine to cross.

the alley receives you into its ordinary chaos — puddles skinned with oil-rainbow, a gutter running fast and loud, steam ghosting up from a grille warm enough to tempt but too open to trust. the drone-thrum stays behind you, walled off, quartering an empty crawlspace it will note as clear. the fry-oil pull strengthens from the east, threaded now with the specific animal warmth of somewhere cats gather. behind you, small and blue and unwatched, your stolen fish turns and turns in a wall no patrol will ever think to look inside — waiting, patient, still yours. ahead, the city hums its one enormous chord. the night, as ever, belongs to whoever moves quietest.

*pause at the mouth of the alley, one paw lifted, whole body a question aimed east.* fry-oil. cat-warmth. the good loud dark. *and behind me, held safe in the wall, the small blue thing that no one gave me and no one can take now that I know the way back to it.* that is enough. that is the whole shape of a good night: something stolen and kept, a patrol outrun, a way home only I know. *paw comes down. ears swivel forward. the hunger picks its direction.* east, then. quiet. always quiet. *and gone into it.*
